clue.text: Made obscure cuts in bestseller's second edition

indicators.note: the cuts sit inside the letters taken from the other words
the second letter of the word bestseller's is the one taken

parts.note: clips are cuts, as in clipping hair or film

explanation.surface: A publisher trimmed a bestseller for its second edition and made it harder to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' picks the second letter of 'bestseller's'; 'in' is the container signal, so the cuts are surrounded rather than following.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to overshadow it, so obscured or made dim is the past tense sense.

clue.text: Run out of passage leading to bar

indicators.note: the run is taken out of the passage

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage taken from a text
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner leaves an alley that leads to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from EXCERPT; 'bar' is the preposition meaning apart from, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, bar and except both mean apart from or excluding.

clue.text: May start when delivery is expected?

definitions.text: May start when delivery is expected?

parts.words: May start when delivery is expected?
parts.note: reads like a pregnant mother whose labour may begin soon; really a holiday falling at the start of the month of May

explanation.walkthrough: May 1 is the workers' holiday in many countries; 'May' looks like the verb and 'delivery' a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The international workers' holiday falls on the first of May, the start of that month.

clue.text: Award — - one accepted by pregnant woman?

indicators.note: the one is taken in, so placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a whimsical coinage: a pre-mum, someone not yet a mother but about to be
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prize for one expectant mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word PRE-MUM; 'accepted by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium is a prize or bonus, an award given as a reward.

clue.text: Hostile soldiers held up by English infantry, finally

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks

indicators.note: the last letter of infantry is taken

explanation.surface: Opposing troops are stopped by the English foot soldiers in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns MEN to NEM in a down clue; 'finally' gives Y, the end of infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, as in enemy aircraft, the word means belonging to a hostile force.

clue.text: 19 represented as Egyptian god

parts.note: 19 is the answer to 19-down, a chemical element; the element whose symbol matches the Egyptian sun god's name is meant

explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry each element is represented by a symbol, and this element's symbol, Ra, is also the name of the Egyptian sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: Its chemical symbol is Ra, the same spelling as the sun god of ancient Egypt, and it is an element.

clue.text: Chopper recovering property stolen by scores of criminals

definitions.text: Chopper recovering property stolen by scores of criminals

parts.words: Chopper recovering property stolen by scores of criminals
parts.note: a woodcutter from the Arabian Nights who took back treasure hidden in a cave by forty thieves, two score of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests an axe or helicopter, but he was a woodcutter; 'scores' hints at forty, the number of thieves in the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor woodcutter of the folk tale found the robbers' cave and carried off their hoard.

clue.text: Man with proof of identity, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: ID is short for identification, proof of who someone is
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A fellow showing his papers, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic expression or mode of speech, a way of putting things.

clue.text: Ring off in the middle of my boring routine

indicators.note: the ring and the off go between the two letters of my

parts.note: O looks like a ring
something off is not on

explanation.surface: Cancelling a call in my tedious day-to-day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle of' puts O and NOT ON inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is wearisome sameness, the dullness of an unchanging routine.

clue.text: Repeatedly try to produce expression of agreement

indicators.note: the word is given more than once, so the piece is doubled

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Keep attempting to get people to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles HEAR, the judge's sense of trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled cry is the traditional shout of approval in Parliament and at meetings.

clue.text: Underground network makes this available on the tube

definitions.text: Underground network makes this available on the tube

parts.words: Underground network makes this available on the tube
parts.note: the surface suggests London's Underground railway, the Tube; really a buried wired network delivering programmes to the TV set, informally the tube

explanation.walkthrough: 'the tube' is British slang for the London Underground but also for television, and the network is buried wiring rather than railway tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription service delivers programmes to viewers' sets through buried wiring, a network beneath the streets.

clue.text: Poverty resulting from pay cut I ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's hardship after their wages were cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges PAY CUT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Paucity is scarcity or a meagre amount, and poverty can likewise mean a lack or deficiency.

clue.text: Allow back into college after study

indicators.note: the college comes after the study in the answer

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, especially at university
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student is let back into college after a period of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is the charade order signal; MIT is the American university, a standard crossword college.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to let them in again, the plain synonym of allowing back.

clue.text: Water provided by disposal of a barrier on river

parts.note: a dam is a barrier built across a river
a sale is a disposal of goods

explanation.surface: Water supplied after a river barrier is sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old jocular phrase for drinking water, since Adam had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous traditional name for plain drinking water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Curly tail as found on an aggressive dog

indicators.note: a curly thing is twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A curled tail seen on a fierce dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curly' is the anagram signal; Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for the German shepherd, a breed known as a guard dog.

clue.text: Boy, after 5, turned to crime

indicators.note: the boy comes after the other piece in the answer
the symbol from 5 is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: 5-across is a chemical element whose symbol is Ra
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster turned to crime after five.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol of the element at 5-across, Ra, is 'turned' to AR, and SON comes 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Daily tranquilliser that's swallowed in the evening

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a downer is a depressant drug

explanation.surface: A sedative taken each day at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a newspaper, here The Sun, a British tabloid; a sundowner is an evening drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken at sunset is something swallowed as the evening begins.

clue.text: Understood one politician agreeing with law

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Someone, a lawmaker, appreciated as law-abiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied without being stated, so tacitly understood.

clue.text: In dismay — befriended, possibly

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is perhaps befriended while in a state of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters run across 'dismay' and 'befriended'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and possibly are both adverbs expressing uncertainty, interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Ideal situation for someone to take lead, for example

definitions.meaning: as in being in one's natural habitat, completely at ease
lead is a metal in the periodic table, one of the basic chemical substances

explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the verb or a leading role, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: One is in one's element when ideally placed, and lead is a chemical one.

clue.text: Female musicians provide stately dance

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name, standing for any female
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A women's group of players performs a dignified dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A girl's name standing for 'Female' is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarabande is a slow, dignified dance in triple time of Spanish origin.

clue.text: Part of theatre in which only the three leading characters may be seen

definitions.text: Part of theatre in which only the three leading characters may be seen

parts.words: Part of theatre in which only the three leading characters may be seen
parts.note: an upper tier of seating, but also the setting of a famous scene with just Cyrano, Christian and Roxane

explanation.walkthrough: In Cyrano de Bergerac's balcony scene only the three principals appear, Cyrano wooing Roxane on Christian's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: This raised gallery of seats in a theatre is also the stage setting of a famous love scene.

clue.text: Swift alias for Esther, say, in South America

indicators.note: the speaking word goes inside the continent's abbreviation

parts.note: to tell is to say

explanation.surface: A fast pseudonym for a woman abroad in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift called Esther Johnson by a pet name in his letters; 'Swift' is the writer, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift's Journal to Stella was addressed to Esther Johnson under this name.

clue.text: Brilliant hit produced by personal aptitude

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash someone
a bent is a natural inclination or talent

explanation.surface: A great success springs from someone's natural talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that glows or flickers softly, hence brilliant or radiant.

clue.text: State of American raised in East?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Was this American brought up in the East?
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AM to MA in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Industrial action contrary to UK law? Not quite!

indicators.note: contrary means going the other way, signalling that the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a strike illegal in Britain? Not really!
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' rearranges TO UK LAW; 'Not quite!' is the setter's wry comment that a strike is not actually unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout is a strike in which workers leave their place of employment in protest.

clue.text: With old-fashioned manner, king is more like Charles V

parts.note: wise is an archaic word for way or manner, as in in no wise
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king with courtly manners is like an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles V of France was known as Charles the Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles V of France was nicknamed the Wise, so resembling him means having greater wisdom.

clue.text: Police's manner is different for such a murder?

indicators.note: the letters are made different, rearranged into new order

parts.note: taken as written including the S

explanation.surface: Detectives handle a certain kind of killing in their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges POLICES MANNER IS; the French phrase means a crime of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names a killing committed in a fit of jealous passion, a kind of murder.

clue.text: Harmonised within limits of Tchaikovsky's score

indicators.note: the harmony word sits inside the outer letters
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: colours that went together harmonised

explanation.surface: Tchaikovsky's music blended within its boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' gives T and Y, the first and last letters of Tchaikovsky's; 'within' puts WENT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, the old counting unit.

clue.text: It's hard to describe precisely where work is inadequate

definitions.meaning: a matter that falls between categories, ill-defined
dated British term for a region of high unemployment, short of jobs but not qualifying as a development area

explanation.walkthrough: In 1960s Britain the phrase named regions with moderate unemployment that missed out on full government aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an ill-defined zone between categories, and was once used for an area with too few jobs.
